text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A maintains clear focal points across two cohesive paragraphs comparing science to other subjects.", "quality": "Paragraph Structure", "description": "Measures the extent to which writing is organized into clear, logical paragraph units rather than long, repetitive blocks of text."}, {"evidence": "Essay A features correct word choices like \"educational,\" \"attention,\" and \"hands on activity,\" whereas Essay B uses flawed words like \"great\" for grade and \"fold\" for fault.", "quality": "Vocabulary Accuracy", "description": "Reflects the correct selection and precise usage of vocabulary words to convey meaning."}, {"evidence": "Essay A displays far fewer severe spelling and word-segmentation errors than Essay B (which includes \"egry,\" \"under Stan,\" \"child rends,\" \"wen,\" and \"Eben\").", "quality": "Spelling Accuracy", "description": "Captures the writer's ability to spell words correctly according to conventional English orthography."}, {"evidence": "Essay A avoids the severe run-on sentences and fractured syntax that dominate Essay B's long paragraphs.", "quality": "Syntactic Control", "description": "Demonstrates command over sentence boundaries and structural clarity to prevent confusing run-on patterns."}]}
